summary:
Held 2 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 4 upside misses — INTC +11%, AMAT +9%, LRCX +7%, COHR +7%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (AKAM -5%, HSY -5%, CIEN -4%, GDDY -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: INTC (+11.19%) — Google placed a firm order for 3M+ TPUs manufactured by Intel's foundry for 2028 delivery, validating its 18A process; Wells Fargo and Barclays also raised price targets on the news. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — INTC is a mega-cap semiconductor not covered by current filters. The move was catalyst-driven (surprise foundry deal disclosed at market open); purely technical overnight signals would show no pre-trade setup.

top_movers.suggestion: Add top-20 semiconductor names by market cap to the universe with a catalyst-gap trigger: release any name printing ≥+5% gap at open on ≥2× avg volume into a short-duration momentum slot on the announcement day.

top_movers.catalyst: Micron confirmed as certified HBM4 supplier for Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform; Wells Fargo reset price target to $1,220 alongside a cluster of analyst upgrades, validating the AI memory supply narrative ahead of June 24 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — MU is a mega-cap semiconductor not included in momentum, mean-reversion, or sector-specific universes. The catalyst (HBM4 certification + analyst target raises of 30-100%+) emerged pre-open, requiring pre-market positioning before the gap was visible in intraday signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add top AI-memory names (MU, MRVL) to macro-aligned's universe with an analyst-upgrade trigger: price-target raise ≥25% on a semi covered by ≥2 desks in the same session fires a pre-open limit order capped at 0.5× normal size.

top_movers.catalyst: Pre-split retail run-up: KLA's 10-for-1 stock split takes effect after June 11 close (announced May 7 alongside Q3 beat of $3.42B vs guidance + 21% dividend hike); June 9 is T-2 before split-adjusted trading begins.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — KLAC trades ~$2,100/share pre-split, almost certainly above nominal price caps in universe construction filters. The move is a corporate-action calendar pattern (split run-up) invisible to momentum/mean-reversion signal logic without an event overlay.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a corporate-action calendar filter that inserts stocks within 5 trading days of a confirmed large-ratio split (≥5:1) into a dedicated catalyst sub-universe, bypassing standard per-share price and ADV floor filters used in universe construction.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 FY2026 earnings beat: revenue $7.9B (vs ~$7.4B est), EPS $3.51 vs $2.63 YoY; Q3 guidance raised to ~$8.95B; dividend increase; AI-driven wafer-fab equipment demand cited.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AMAT is a mega-cap semiconductor equipment name not in any current watchlist. The 8.64% move was an earnings gap-up requiring either pre-results positioning or a same-session earnings-reactive entry the bot currently lacks.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-release rule that makes large-cap semis-equipment names (AMAT, LRCX, KLAC) eligible for a momentum entry when post-results intraday gap ≥+5% and volume ≥2× 30-day avg within the first 30 minutes of open.

top_movers.catalyst: UBS raised LRCX price target to $375 from $310 (Buy reiterated) on AI-driven wafer fab equipment demand; amplified by Nvidia Computex AI chip cycle tailwinds and a strong fiscal Q3 2026 earnings beat.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LRCX is a large-cap semi equipment name (~$45B cap). Catalyst was a sell-side PT upgrade announced pre-market; the −7.5% drop on Jun 5 would also have tripped short-term volatility-exclusion filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a sell-side upgrade scanner: when a Tier-1 bank raises PT ≥15% on a semi equipment name and shares open gap-up ≥3%, allow momentum entry in the first 30 min regardless of prior-session drawdown recency.

top_movers.catalyst: Nvidia's $2B equity investment + multibillion-dollar AI optics purchase commitment (announced ~May 26) drove a structural re-rating; Jun 9 +6.62% is a secondary bounce off post-ATH pullback ($440 Jun 3 → $377 → $402) as AI datacenter demand narrative holds.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. COHR ($73B market cap, AI photonics) made its +30% primary move on the Nvidia $2B deal by Jun 3; Jun 9 is a secondary bounce leg that post-gap momentum filters likely excluded due to extended RSI and prior-session ATH overhang.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap AI-infrastructure names (e.g. COHR) to a post-catalyst continuation universe gated by: gap ≥+20% in prior 5 sessions AND RSI < 70 on entry day, to capture secondary bounces without chasing the initial spike.

top_movers.catalyst: Profit-taking and valuation reset after a +62% YTD AI-infrastructure rally; compounded by Zacks 'Strong Sell' downgrade (May 21) and Q2 EPS estimate cuts — no discrete new catalyst on the day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AKAM is a large-cap NASDAQ infra name (~$9B). The decline was slow-building valuation compression (P/E 47.8x vs 5yr median 27.9x), not a tradable gap or volume spike detectable intraday.

top_movers.catalyst: Multiple banks cut HSY price targets on June 9 (Mizuho to $185, UBS to $200, JPMorgan to $204, BofA to $220) on top of ~50k Hershey Trust insider shares sold June 1–5, intensifying margin-pressure concerns from elevated cocoa costs.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — HSY is a large-cap defensive consumer staples name (~$24B mkt cap). The decline was analyst-downgrade- and insider-flow-driven with no pre-market gap or volume spike that a momentum or news-reactive screener would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an analyst-action scanner: flag names where ≥2 banks cut price targets on the same session day and Form-4 insider sales appear within the prior 5 sessions; route flagged names to a short-bias news-reactive sub-strategy with a 1-day holding period.

top_movers.catalyst: Ciena priced a $2.5B (upsized from $2B) 0%-coupon convertible senior notes due 2031 on June 8-9; the dilutive capital raise — announced days after a strong Q2 earnings beat — triggered the ~4.4% sell-off.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — CIEN is a large-cap optical networking equipment name (~$466/share). The trigger was a same-day capital-markets event (convertible offering via 8-K filing); no pre-market momentum or mean-reversion signal existed to flag it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a real-time SEC 8-K monitor for convertible-note and secondary-offering filings across large-cap tech-adjacent names; auto-flag intraday short exposure when the dilutive issuance principal exceeds ~5% of the issuer's market cap.

top_movers.catalyst: Ongoing securities law investigation (Kaplan Fox probe) into GoDaddy's disclosures around a dotcom promotional pricing misstep that reduced near-term bookings, compounded by FY2026 revenue guidance ($5.20–5.28B) falling just below the $5.29B consensus.
